page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v7 is an x86_64 instance built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, utilizing the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU architecture provides 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, supported by instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA_NI. System memory totals 64.0 GB, resulting in a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage is bundled with an integrated 1888 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance operates without a discrete GPU accelerator.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong compute characteristics driven by the 4.5 GHz core frequency. In stress-ng single-core execution, the instance scores in the top 10%, complemented by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression throughput. PassMark evaluations record strong scores across CPU compute, extended instructions, cryptographic throughput, and physics simulations. Memory subsystem tests yield median performance, showing 107.09 GB/sec uncached read and 72.68 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth. In operational tests, Redis reaches 53.41 million SET operations per second, static web serving measures 43.7 GB/sec, and text generation on small 135M parameter language models achieves top-tier throughput at 404.59 tokens per second.

The 1:2 memory-to-core ratio of the D32alds_v7 provides qualitative cost efficiency for compute-focused tasks that do not demand extensive RAM footprints. A significant advantage is the bundled 1888 GB NVMe SSD, which supplies high-speed local scratch space without requiring additional network-attached block volumes. The primary tradeoff is the constrained 64 GB memory capacity, which limits viability for large in-memory caching layers or enterprise databases. The server is suited for CPU-heavy batch workloads, software compilation and CI/CD pipelines, compression tasks, web serving, and disk-intensive ETL operations.
description: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, it supplies 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores alongside 64 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation. The configuration includes a bundled 1888 GB local NVMe SSD for fast ephemeral storage and operates without an attached GPU. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core stress-ng performance and leading compression throughput via gzip and bzip3. Its high clock speed yields strong PassMark CPU and cryptographic scores, while memory bandwidth and multi-core stress metrics perform in the median range. The compact memory footprint per core makes it cost-efficient for compute-dense workloads rather than memory-heavy software. The instance is suited for batch processing, build and CI/CD pipelines, web serving, and local disk-intensive data transformations.
